subject: occupancy model example (single season, no covariates)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: occupancy model example (single season, no covariates)
parts:
I was too tired to write more C++, so I coded the
occupancy model translated from Marc Kery's WinBUGS model here:

http://www.fisheriesstockassessment.com/TikiWiki/tiki-index.php?page=BUGS+Occupancy

which is itself based on Royle and Kery's 2007 paper:

http://www.fisheriesstockassessment.com/files/RoyleKery2007.pdf

I've attached the R simulator and Stan model. But they're
small enough to also just include in the e-mail body; the
fit using RStan 2.1.0 is below.


R simulator
----------------------------------------
R <- 250;
T <- 10;
p <- 0.55;
psi <- 0.4;

z <- rbinom(R,1,psi);

y <- matrix(NA,R,T);
for (r in 1:R)
y[r,] <- rbinom(T,1,z[r] * p);



Stan model
-------------------------------------
data {
int<lower=0> R;
int<lower=0> T;
int<lower=0,upper=1> y[R,T];
}
parameters {
real<lower=0,upper=1> psi1;
real<lower=0,upper=1> p;
}
model {
// local variables to avoid recomputing log(psi1) and log(1 - psi1)
real log_psi1;
real log1m_psi1;
log_psi1 <- log(psi1);
log1m_psi1 <- log1m(psi1);

// priors
psi1 ~ uniform(0,1);
p ~ uniform(0,1);

// likelihood
for (r in 1:R) {
if (sum(y[r]) > 0)
increment_log_prob(log_psi1 + bernoulli_log(y[r],p));
else
increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(log_psi1 + bernoulli_log(y[r],p),
log1m_psi1));
}
}


The model's more verbose than it needs to be because
I cached log(psi1) and log(1 - psi1) to avoid recomputing.
I also included the uniform(0,1) priors just to be explicit,
but these can be dropped --- they're implicitly specified by
the constraints on p and psi1.

Rhats and effective sample sizes are very good and the traceplots
show it converges from diffuse starting points in a handful of iterations.

I hope it isn't hard to extend this to covariates --- the tricky part
is the marginalization which the above model has.

I'm going to include this in the next version of the manual
along with the Cormack-Jolly-Seber mark-recapture models.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: occupancy model example (single season, no covariates)
parts:
Glad you got it to work and thanks for sharing your model.

I only see one place you could make things more efficient:

for (r in 1:R) {
psi[r] <- inv_logit(B0 + B_x1*x1[r] + B_x2*x2[r]);
for (j in 1:J) p[r,j] <- inv_logit(A0 + A_x1*x1[r]);
}

It's counter-intuitive, but it would help if you made
a B_x1_times_x1 vector and so on.

The first one would be to declare a new transformed parameter

vector[R] B_x1_times_x1;

and then define it as

B_x1_times_x1 <- B_x1 * x1;

and then replace the use of B_x1*x1[r] with B_x1_times_x1[r].
You can do the same thing with the other products.

Next, you can use bernoulli_logit_log, which is defined by:

bernoulli_logit_log(u, q) = bernoulli_log(u, inverse_logit(q))

Then you don't have to define p, you can just define

for (j in 1:J) logit_p[r,j] <- A0 + A_x1*x1[r];

And then you can vectorize this to:

logit_p[r] <- A0 + A_x1 * x1;

It's also more arithmetically stable doing it this way.

- Bob
